title: 35 Clips, One Look: Killing My Repeat Template | vitalii.no
description:
How a batch of 35 feature-demo videos ended up with one identical staging — and the fix that made every clip since look genuinely different.

Every one of my 35 bright feature-demo clips, rendered over about a week, used the exact same staging: centered headline, red and green zone panels, three icon cards, two result cards, the same color palette and the same four-beat rhythm. Thirty-five completely different product stories ended up looking like one repeated video. The sameness wasn't a limitation of the renderer — it was baked into the batch instructions that told every agent to copy one reference file exactly.

The fix rewrote those instructions. Before writing any clip, an agent now computes an index from the feature's own id against a table of eight staging archetypes, and steps to the next one whenever the computed archetype matches either of the last two logged in an archetype history file — so no two features in the same batch ever share a staging. The color system grew from one fixed palette to five, exposed through a shared context so every layout element can pick it up automatically.

Six new clips went out under the new system, each with a distinct archetype and mood with no repeats across the batch, verified frame-by-frame and confirmed live on the public video URLs with no database or publishing code changes required.
